clue.text: Retreating sailors protected by Irish front line

indicators.note: the Irish letters surround and shelter the sailors, putting them inside

parts.note: the front two letters of Irish, also the standard abbreviation for Irish

indicators.note: sailors retreating go backwards, so the pair is read in reverse

parts.note: AB is an able seaman and OS an ordinary seaman, together sailors

explanation.surface: A boat crew backs off behind an Irish defensive front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front line' reads as one military phrase, but 'Irish front' gives the wordplay letters and 'line' alone is the definition, a line on a weather map.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather chart joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: An apostle not entirely visible in Chinese republic

indicators.note: the apostle and An are to be seen inside the Chinese letters

parts.note: SINO- is the prefix meaning Chinese

indicators.note: only part of the apostle's name is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Mark, one of the gospel writers, called an apostle here

explanation.surface: A saint's figure is only partly on view in some Chinese republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese republic' looks like one phrase naming China; the definition is just 'republic', and 'Chinese' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: Support or express contempt for Knotty Ash comedian, not funny

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in contempt

indicators.note: the comedian's name goes without the letters meaning funny, so they are removed

parts.note: Ken Dodd, the British comedian famous for his fictional Knotty Ash, a Liverpool suburb
funny in the sense of strange, odd

explanation.surface: Someone backs or jeers a famously unfunny Liverpool comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a British comedian forever associated with Knotty Ash, a Liverpool suburb; calling him 'not funny' is the joke, as 'funny' means odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookend is a support placed at the end of a row of books to keep them upright.

clue.text: Carried aboard British ships, Sandinista finally took flight

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the ships, as cargo carried aboard

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a Nicaraguan revolutionary; its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A Nicaraguan rebel, carried on British warships, eventually escaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran is the past tense of run, which means fled, the same as took flight.

clue.text: Cook cut round plant brought to a mature woman

indicators.note: the plant group is brought next to the following letter
the shortened cooking word goes round the plant
the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to bake is to cook
a bush is a plant

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: trim a plant and serve it to an older lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as a command in a recipe, but it supplies the baking verb, which is then shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Babushka is Russian for grandmother, used for an elderly or old woman.

clue.text: Immature, getting in middle of clubland fight

indicators.note: the immature word goes into the middle letters
only the central pair of letters of the word is used

parts.note: the source for the central letters
raw means inexperienced, immature

explanation.surface: A green youngster gets caught up in a scrap in the nightclub district.
explanation.walkthrough: Clubland has eight letters, so its middle is the two central ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a noisy, rough fight or scuffle.

clue.text: Man, not the Messiah, on cold Irish water? He managed

parts.note: from Monty Python's Life of Brian: 'He's not the Messiah, he's a very naughty boy'
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a lough is an Irish lake

explanation.surface: A man insists he is no Messiah while standing on a cold Irish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Life of Brian is a Monty Python film whose hero is told he is not the Messiah. Brian Clough was a famous English football manager, of Derby and Nottingham Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Clough was a celebrated football manager who won the European Cup twice with Nottingham Forest.

clue.text: Trying to excise mass — no significant growth

indicators.note: the letter for mass is cut out of the trying word

parts.note: sampling means trying, as of food
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A bid to remove a lump ends with the reassuring news there is no notable growth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a medical report on a tumour; the definition is a playful description of a young tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapling is a young tree, still too small to count as substantial growth.

clue.text: Suffering regular losses, upset farmer lacks destiny

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the kept letters upside down, reading them backwards
every other letter of the following words is lost, leaving the alternate ones

parts.note: the stretch whose even letters are kept

explanation.surface: A struggling farmer, hit by repeated losses, finds fortune has deserted him.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of 'farmer lacks' gives AMRAK, which 'upset' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Karma, in Hindu and Buddhist belief, is the force of one's actions shaping one's fate.

clue.text: Problem at retirement at home as I'm on for working

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pensioner's grumble: retirement's trouble is that one keeps working from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' reads as leaving a job, but here it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is sleeplessness, a problem when one turns in for the night.

clue.text: Goods in from overseas having considerable weight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: foreign goods brought into a country

explanation.surface: Foreign merchandise that carries real weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Import is both a product brought from abroad and a formal word for significance or consequence.

clue.text: Fruit plant soils weren't loam

indicators.note: to soil is to dirty or mess up, so the letters are messed into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A gardener complains a fruit crop dirtied beds that weren't proper loam.
explanation.definitionFit: The watermelon is a trailing vine grown for its large juicy fruit.

clue.text: Create as legend heartless moggy, hostile, running amok

indicators.note: the combined letters run wild into a new order
the central letter of the cat word is removed

parts.note: British slang for a cat; here just the word's letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone turns a ferocious, rampaging cat into folklore.
explanation.walkthrough: Moggy loses its middle G to give MOGY, and MOGY + HOSTILE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To mythologise is to turn something into myth, making it the stuff of tales.

clue.text: Maybe single mother becomes prayer leader

parts.note: one is an example of single, and I is the Roman numeral one
mam is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A lone parent takes on a role leading worship.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the person who leads the prayers in a mosque.

clue.text: Beer leads to madness in local discotheque

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Drinking leads to crazy behaviour in a nearby nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild is a British dark ale, lightly hopped and low in strength.

clue.text: Devout student in times past collecting old Christian sayings

indicators.note: the past-time word gathers the others inside it

parts.note: then means at that past time
logia are sayings attributed to Jesus

explanation.surface: A pious scholar in former days compiled old Christian sayings.
explanation.walkthrough: Logia (singular logion) are collected sayings of Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: A theologian is a scholar of religion and God, so a student of the divine.

clue.text: City bank devoid of capital

indicators.note: the word loses its capital, i.e. its first letter

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A city's bank has run out of funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' and 'capital' look financial: bank is the verb rely, and capital is its head letter. Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely is a small English city in Cambridgeshire, famed for its cathedral.

clue.text: Spanish region with a mostly luxurious island area

parts.note: and means together with

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: lush means luxurious, opulent

explanation.surface: A Spanish region comes with a largely luxurious island district.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is the southernmost autonomous community of Spain, home to Seville and Granada.

clue.text: Vegetables are supposed to be this well done

definitions.text: Vegetables are supposed to be this

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an exclamation of congratulation

explanation.surface: Greens should be good for you, and properly cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well done' looks like cooking instructions for vegetables; it is the cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes healthy food and is also said to praise someone's achievement.

clue.text: Threatening to have party for graduate experiencing sorrow

indicators.note: the threatening word is made to have something new
one thing stands for another, swapping out the graduate

parts.note: baleful means menacing
BA is a Bachelor of Arts
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone threatens to throw a party to celebrate a graduate in mourning.
explanation.walkthrough: BALEFUL swaps its BA for DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Doleful means mournful, full of sorrow and grief.

clue.text: Germ linked to eastern seaside resort

indicators.note: the two parts are joined in sequence

parts.note: a germ is a bud or seed of growth

explanation.surface: A bug traced to a resort on the east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Bude is a seaside town in Cornwall, in fact on England's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Bude is a Cornish seaside town known for its beaches and surfing.

clue.text: Get intoxicated long after beer has run out

indicators.note: the longing word comes after the other
the run letter is out, taken from the beer word

parts.note: a brew is a beer
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to itch is to long for

explanation.surface: A drinker gets drunk, still craving more after the beer is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out' looks like supplies ending; it is R (run) leaving BREW.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewitch is to enchant or captivate, making someone heady and intoxicated, as if spellbound.

clue.text: Fish leaving river — cost measured in lives?

indicators.note: the river letter departs from the fishing word

parts.note: to troll is to fish by trailing a line

explanation.surface: An angler quits the river, wondering about the human price.
explanation.definitionFit: A death toll is the number of people killed, the price of a disaster in human lives.

clue.text: So dramatic, with lunar eclipse at last revealing earth's shade

indicators.note: the final letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A dramatic lunar eclipse reveals the colour our planet casts on the Moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth's shade' suggests Earth's shadow in an eclipse; it is a colour of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a natural earth pigment, giving a yellow to brownish colour.

clue.text: Unconventional Olympian climbers potentially falling thus?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: sport climbers might literally fall off the climbing wall

explanation.walkthrough: Sport climbing became an Olympic event in 2021; competitors climb artificial walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-wall is slang for zany or eccentric, and literally where a falling wall climber ends up.

clue.text: Go hungry, retaining little energy: address that here?

indicators.note: the hunger word keeps the energy letter within it

parts.note: to fast is to go without food
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: Someone starving and low on energy is told where to deal with that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address that' means deal with the hunger just mentioned: a banquet is where to do it.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a lavish meal, the place to tackle hunger head on.

clue.text: Butcher's fine cuts secure starter for Indian

indicators.note: the fine letter cuts into the secure word

parts.note: to shut is to close securely
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

parts.note: source of the starting letter

explanation.surface: A butcher cuts fine meat and secures the first course for an Indian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is Cockney rhyming slang for a look (butcher's hook); a shufti is also British slang for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: Shufti is British slang, from Arabic, meaning a quick glance, the same as having a butcher's.

clue.text: Renouncing faith in second year after ex-drinkers outside bar

indicators.note: second and year follow the rest
the ex-drinkers go outside the bar

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, for those who have given up drink
a post is a bar, as in a goalpost

explanation.surface: In their second year, former drinkers stay outside the pub and lose faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' tempts as a pub beside the ex-drinkers; it is POST.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostasy is the abandonment of a religious belief.

clue.text: Eggs from hen — six delivered for picking up?

indicators.note: picking up sound, as by ear, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls delivered by a bowler

explanation.surface: A batch of half a dozen eggs from a hen is ready to collect.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the plural of ovum, a female egg cell.

clue.text: What will punter do to acquire new set at any cost?

indicators.note: the gambler's phrase takes in the new letter

parts.note: he'll bet: what a gambler will do

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a gambler will do to get a fresh set, whatever the price.
explanation.walkthrough: The question is answered by HE'LL BET, which takes in N.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent means utterly determined, regardless of the consequences.

clue.text: Holy man residing here has made spicy butter

indicators.note: spicing up mixes things around, rearranging the letters

parts.note: the anagram fodder
a ram is an animal that butts

explanation.surface: A guru's home has whipped up spiced butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' suggests the dairy spread; it is a ram, one that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu hermitage or retreat where a guru lives with followers.
